context: The sorted integer array is nums = [1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 10, 12, 15]. The target value 6 (target = 6) occupies indices 2 through 6. Since all elements are integers, neither target - 0.5 = 5.5 nor target + 0.5 = 6.5 can occur in the array.
description: When a closed-interval binary search looks for an absent value, it never takes the equality branch. Once the interval is empty, i points to the first element greater than the search value, and j to the rightmost element less than it. If there is no greater element, i = n. If there is no smaller element, j = −1. In each case the corresponding pointer is outside the array.

The left panel shows how finding the leftmost target is equivalent to searching for target - 0.5 (5.5). The search ends with j = 1 at the value 3 and i = 2 at the first element greater than 5.5, the leftmost 6. Returning i = 2 gives the left boundary. The right panel shows how finding the rightmost target is equivalent to searching for target + 0.5 (6.5). The search ends with j = 6 at the rightmost element less than 6.5, the last 6, and i = 7 at the value 10. Returning j = 6 gives the right boundary.

frames.explanation: This method depends on all elements being integers. If the array contains fractional values, adding or subtracting 0.5 could produce an existing element and invalidate the method. In a general implementation where target may be absent, verify that the index is in bounds and the element equals target before returning it.
frames.title: Finding left and right boundaries using half-integers

summary: In an integer array, search for two half-integers that cannot occur in the array to locate the boundaries of a repeated value.
title: Finding left and right boundaries using half-integers
